# CMV COLITIS OR ESOPHAGITIS

Infection in immunocompetent patients is rare and usually associated with minimal or no symptoms. Patients in whom the risk for CMV disease is increased include solid organ and bone marrow transplant recipients, persons receiving prolonged immunosuppressive chemotherapy, and persons with advanced HIV disease indicated by a CD4 count of less than 50 cells/microliter. Treatment is complex and requires Infectious Diseases consultation.

## Duration of therapy

Treat for 3-6 weeks. Patients may be converted to oral therapy after initial intravenous therapy and after clinical improvement of severe disease.

## Treatment of severe disease

Refer to Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS.
References:

- Guidelines for Prevention and Treatment of Opportunistic Infections in HIV
- Infected Adults and Adolescents. AIDSinfo (2015) 1-282
- Mandell chapter: Cytomegalovirus
- Sanford keyword: Cytomegalovirus
- Up-to-Date article: Epidemiology, clinical manifestations, and treatment of cytomegalovirus infection in immunocompetent adults
Therapy:
## Treatment of mild to moderate disease or following clinical improvement of severe disease

## Inpatient

Valganciclovir 900 mg PO q12h [R,O]

## Treatment of severe disease

Ganciclovir 5 mg/kg IV q12h [R,O]
< OR >
Foscarnet 90 mg/kg IV q12h [R,O]

## Outpatient

Valganciclovir 900 mg PO BID ($$$) [R,O]
Non-VA order for above
Inpt: ORZID2 GMENU ABX CMV COLITIS OR ESOPHAGITIS
